feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear domain positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector scope. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond activity/scale metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is logical and credible, culminating in director-level ownership of platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Strong relevance and specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, AI-enabled search, and public-sector communications create a focused, modern profile.  
- Good evidence of scale: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and newsletter reach help establish scope.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome metrics: include business/user impact such as engagement growth, conversion improvements, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption results—not just responsibilities and platform scale.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve scannability and save space.  
- Minor style/consistency fixes: “organization-wide” is preferable to “organization wide”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs versions without it); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the experience section, but it’s slightly dense and repeats several ideas already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and skills sections. It would be stronger with sharper phrasing and one or two concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and modernize the opening: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience building the systems, governance, and content operations behind large-scale public-sector communications.”
- Replace “high-volume” with a more specific phrase such as “large-scale” or “high-traffic” to sound clearer and less generic.
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “multi-channel platforms serving public-sector stakeholders.”
- Streamline the second sentence to reduce list fatigue: “Leads web modernization, analytics, editorial infrastructure, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” would be more specific.
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; consider varying the wording.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing functions, channels, and outcomes in one list.
- Prioritize the strongest recent differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, AI search, automation/integration, and multimedia operations.
- Consider replacing “Advocacy and public-sector communications” with a more capability-based phrase such as “Public-sector digital communications” for consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel digital communications • Public-sector digital communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; if both remain, keep this section high-level and let Topline Skills carry the tools/platform detail.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and “Advocacy/public-sector communications” are both reinforced in multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [thing] using [methods/features] to [outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future expansion”; spell out “10 × 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this phrasing: “Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current and NACo role bullets.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “production and distribution,” and Drupal microsite details echo existing skills/experience sections.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and lead with impact: “Built and optimized digital systems, workflows, and analytics to improve coordination across enterprise communications.”
- Make Drupal/web work more outcome-focused: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Tighten the technical/AI bullets: “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties and led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite examples already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.
- Governance/analytics language overlaps with prior NACo roles and the summary; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, % efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production cost savings, or engagement growth from the studio and analytics work.
- Tighten weaker phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels...” with specifics on volume, growth, engagement, or campaign results.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video channel management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and governance here.
- Video production also appears in older NACo roles; keep this version focused on building the in-house studio as a strategic capacity upgrade.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational ownership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across multiple internal teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and include views, open rates, or production cadence if available.
- Rephrase vague bullets with concrete systems impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes connecting communications, advocacy and program staff” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the footer project and 2015–2018 role; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director entry.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:

- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability areas: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”

- Put the strongest, more current tools first; if Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions are recent hands-on tools, move them ahead of jQuery.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., automation, deployment, or performance improvements enabled by these tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; consider trimming one section or making this version more implementation-specific.
- GTM may overlap with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if you actively implemented tagging, not just managed analytics.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems

- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; include only if they support a broader workflow/operations story

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given your recent leadership over email/newsletter operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list. It would be stronger if framed around capability and aligned to the platforms most clearly supported by your experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **email campaign delivery, member communications, and engagement workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding metrics here like “tens of thousands of subscribers”; that’s already stronger in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims elsewhere, so anchor this item specifically to **email/member platform systems**.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this line is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should be tighter, more tool-led, and avoid broad capability terms unless they add specificity.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**

- If true, add one higher-value specialty instead of a generic term: **tagging/measurement strategy**, **conversion analysis**, or **behavior analytics**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader strategy language elsewhere without showing a distinct technical tool or method.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer

Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
